## Formal {.unnumbered}
Adding a scalar
Adding a matrix M means M + 1 = M were each entry is added 1

Multiplying a scalar means that M * 2 = where each entry is multiplied by 2

Adding two matrices
This is a special case, and the simplest is matrix of same dimension, so that M + L = adding each entry

Multiply two matrices (Hadamard product)

The advantage is that it is commutative
M + 1 = 1 + M
M * 2 = 2 * M

It is also associative
M + L + K = M + K + L

And distributive

This is a desired feature where the + and * have kept their original meaning.
